children: South Korean companies are showing a widening split, with large firms posting a sharp jump in exports while small and medium-sized businesses saw production decline. According to Sina Finance, Samsung Electronics continues to report record-high results, and semiconductor-sector enthusiasm remains elevated, but the gains have not spread to South Korea's smaller companies.

According to data released on the 11th by South Korea's national statistics portal KOSIS, small and medium-sized manufacturers posted a production index of 83.9 in August, down 4% from a year earlier. Large-company production index was 118.6, down 1.8% year on year.

Export performance also diverged. According to South Korea's Customs Service, large-company exports totaled $77.1 billion in August, up 94.2% from a year earlier, while small and medium-sized company exports were $10.1 billion, up 20.4%. From January to August, large-company exports reached $517.3 billion, up 74.4%, compared with $83.3 billion for small and medium-sized companies, up 14.8%.

The wage gap between large and small firms also continued to widen. According to South Korea's Ministry of Employment and Labor corporate labor survey, the average monthly wage for employees at companies with 300 or more regular workers was 6.49 million won in July, compared with 3.846 million won at companies with fewer than 300 workers. The wage ratio between large firms and small and medium-sized firms rose to 1.69 times from 1.66 times a year earlier.

title: South Korean Firms Diverge as Large-Company Exports Surge and Small-Business Output Falls
